html:
The Romanian War of Independence was Romania's part in the Russo-Turkish War, in which it declared independence from the Ottoman Empire on 21 May 1877 and fought beside Russia.

Romanian troops crossed the Danube and helped Russia besiege the Ottoman fortress of Plevna in Bulgaria, which fell in December 1877 after months of fighting. At the Congress of Berlin in 1878 the powers recognised Romania's independence. Romania gained northern Dobruja with the port of Constanța but had to give southern Bessarabia back to Russia, its ally, which caused lasting bitterness. Carol I was crowned king in 1881. The war is the founding military story of modern Romania.
